scenario: AITA for letting my (33M) best friend (33F) stay overnight at my place after she had a fight with her husband? | Jess and I have been friends since we were in the first grade. When we were teenagers, I developed the biggest crush on her. Unfortunately, when I confessed my feelings to her, she turned me down, and told me she only ever saw me as a friend. It broke my heart, but we continued being good friends anyway, hanging out after school, going to anime cosplays conventions and other geeky stuff. We kinda grew apart after high school and went to different universities. Though we weren't close anymore, we still call each other occasionally and hanging out over the summer holidays. Jess started dating Andy during her senior year, and married him a year after she graduated. As for me, I realized I was gay and have only been in romantic relationships with men since. Years past, and one day, I got a call from Jess. She was crying. She said she just got into a fight with Andy. She asked if she could come over because she didn't feel safe at home. I freaked out, thinking she was in danger, so I told her to come over to my apartment asap and I'll meet her at the lobby to greet her. I thought that the security at my apartment would keep her safe if her husband was planning to do anything to her. When she got to my apartment, she was mess. She was crying and everything. I told her she could stay with me while she got things settled down. I had an extra bedroom, that is use as a guest bedroom when my parents are in town. We ended up hugging on the couch, while she was crying on and off. She suddenly told me how she wished she had reciprocated my feelings before when I confessed my feelings years ago but didn't dare to because she didn't want to ruin our friendship. I told her honestly that I'll always be her friend. The romantic feelings I had for her had faded a long time ago. I'm now seeing someone, and things between he and I are getting serious. But she is still welcome to stay in the guest bedroom until things settled down. I was bothered by what had happened that night. I confided in my partner (the same one as above) and he said I was an asshole for letting her stay over. He said while he has nothing against it, it's socially inappropriate for a single man to allow married woman to spend the night as his place. What did I expect was going to happen? I could've ruin Jess' marriage with Andy. Not asking for relationship advice. Just want to know if I am really an asshole for helping out a married friend.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether letting my best friend Jess stay overnight at my place after she had a fight with her husband is considered AITA (Am I The Asshole). Let me break this down step by step. First, Jess and I have been friends since first grade. That's a really long time, and we've been through a lot together. When we were teenagers, I had a crush on her, but she turned me down, saying she only saw me as a friend. That was really hard for me, but we managed to stay friends. We did a lot of fun things together, like going to anime conventions and other geeky stuff. After high school, we grew apart a bit because we went to different universities, but we still kept in touch, especially during summer holidays. Jess started dating Andy during her senior year and married him a year after she graduated. For me, I realized I was gay and have only been in relationships with men since then. So, I've moved on from any romantic feelings towards Jess. Now, the situation is that Jess called me one day, really upset, saying she had a fight with Andy and didn't feel safe at home. She asked if she could come over. I was worried she was in danger, so I told her to come to my apartment and I'd meet her at the lobby. I thought the security at my place would keep her safe if Andy was planning anything. When she arrived, she was a mess, crying and everything. I told her she could stay in the guest bedroom while she sorted things out. We ended up hugging on the couch, and she mentioned how she wished she had reciprocated my feelings back then but didn't want to ruin our friendship. I reassured her that I'm still her friend, and the romantic feelings I had for her have faded. I'm now seeing someone, and things are getting serious, but she's still welcome to stay until things settle down. However, I'm feeling bothered by what happened that night. I confided in my partner, who said I was an asshole for letting her stay over. He mentioned that it's socially inappropriate for a single man to allow a married woman to spend the night at his place, and I could have ruined Jess's marriage with Andy. I'm not asking for relationship advice, just whether I was really an asshole for helping out a married friend. So, is it right or wrong for me to let Jess stay overnight? Let's think about the different aspects. First, Jess was in a vulnerable state, feeling unsafe at home. As a friend, I wanted to help her. Offering her a place to stay seemed like the right thing to do, especially since I was worried about her safety. I didn't see any immediate danger, but I wanted to ensure she was safe. Second, I have a romantic history with Jess, but I've moved on, and she knows that. I'm now in a serious relationship with someone else, and I told her that the romantic feelings I had for her have faded. So, there shouldn't be any romantic intentions on my part. Third, my partner thinks it's socially inappropriate for a single man to allow a married woman to stay overnight. He's worried that it could lead to misunderstandings or even ruin Jess's marriage. But I didn't have any intentions of causing harm; I just wanted to help a friend in need. On the other hand, maybe there's a risk of overstepping boundaries. Even though I have no romantic feelings, others might interpret the situation differently. My partner's concern is valid in that sense. But ultimately, I was trying to help Jess during a difficult time. I didn't have any ulterior motives, and I made sure to communicate clearly that I'm still her friend. So, was I really an asshole for doing that? I think it's important to consider the intent behind my actions. I was genuinely trying to help a friend who was in distress. I didn't see any harm in offering her a safe place to stay, especially since I have a guest bedroom. I also made sure to maintain appropriate boundaries by having her stay in a separate room and not engaging in any romantic behavior. However, I can understand why my partner might be concerned about the social implications. It's a tricky situation because even if there are no romantic intentions, others might interpret it differently. But I think as long as I was clear about my intentions and maintained appropriate boundaries, it wasn't wrong to help Jess. In conclusion, while there might be some social concerns, my primary intent was to support a friend in need. As long as I communicated clearly and maintained appropriate boundaries, I don't think I was an asshole for letting Jess stay overnight.
